evidence.question: Is the dividend safe?
evidence.text: Short answer: the data doesn't say whether it's "safe" — but on what's published, the payout has been raised or held in every quarter over the last two years, the yield is 5.23%, and the balance-sheet gauges the database does publish (debt/equity 0.2006, current ratio 1.9986) look comfortable P1Key metrics DB. The key coverage measures — payout ratio, free-cash-flow yield, interest coverage — are not available in this database, so the earnings-vs-cash test can't be run here.Track record (SAR per share, quarterly)- The most recent declared dividend is SAR 0.34 (Q2 2026, announced 2026-08-04, ex-date 2026-08-19, paid 2026-08-27), up from SAR 0.33 in each of the four quarters of 2025 DB.- Before that, Q1–Q3 2024 quarters carried SAR 0.48, and Q4 2024 dropped to SAR 0.33 DB.- The size of those payments was SAR 82,060 million (Q2 2026), SAR 82,080 million (Q1 2026), SAR 82,080 million (Q4 2025) and SAR 80,120 million (Q3 2025) — roughly SAR 326,340 million over the last four declared quarters DB.- The step-down from SAR 0.48 to SAR 0.33 was in the performance-linked component, not the base: the 2024 quarters included performance-linked dividends of SAR 40,390–40,410 million, while the 2025 quarters included only SAR 820 million of performance-linked dividends, and the 2026 quarters carry no such note DB.What the income and health data shows- Dividend yield 5.23% on a last price of SAR 25.48 as of 2026-10-20; EPS (TTM) SAR 1.84; P/E 13.86x; ROE 26.75%; ROA 15.86% P1Key metrics.- Debt/equity 0.2006 (54th sector percentile) and current ratio 1.9986 (68.7th percentile), with a health group score of 61.35 DB.- Payout ratio, interest coverage and free-cash-flow yield are not published for this ticker — payout shows "missing inputs", interest coverage "missing inputs", and fcf_yield is not applicable for the sector DB. So cash-cost coverage of the ~SAR 326bn annual outflow cannot be measured from this data.- One structural note: a March 2026 disclosure records board approval to buy back up to 350 million shares (max SAR 11.3 billion) for an employee share plan, funded from internal funds DB.Council and news read- On the AlphaCouncil as of 2026-10-16, the income seat voted bullish (yield above the 5% threshold) and the risk seat bullish (1-year volatility 14.78% with a yield above 3%), alongside bullish quality and neutral value; momentum was bearish and news abstained DB.- Timeliness caveat: the disclosures and news feed for this ticker is stale — its newest item is dated 2026-03-09 — so any dividend announcement after that date would not appear here P1Key metrics.This is a description of the published data, not a recommendation on the shares.Saudi Aramco (2222) — dividend history, SAR per shareget_dividends(2222)Pin to dashboardQuarterAnnouncedEx-datePay dateDPS (SAR)Amount (SAR mn)Q2 20262026-08-042026-08-192026-08-270.3482,060Q1 20262026-05-102026-06-012026-06-090.3482,080Q4 20252026-03-102026-03-162026-03-310.3482,080Q3 20252025-11-042025-11-172025-11-260.3380,120Q2 20252025-08-052025-08-192025-08-280.3380,110Q1 20252025-05-112025-05-212025-05-290.3380,110Q4 20242025-03-042025-03-172025-03-260.3380,100Q3 20242024-11-052024-11-142024-11-260.48116,450Q2 20242024-08-062024-08-202024-08-290.48116,450Q1 20242024-05-072024-05-142024-05-230.48116,510

evidence.question: How does the valuation compare with its peers?
evidence.text: Saudi Aramco sits mid-pack on earnings multiple (P/E 13.86x vs a peer range of 5.14x–28.20x) but is the most expensive of the group on price-to-book (3.93x vs 1.48x–2.68x), while offering the highest dividend yield (5.23%) and by far the largest scale at SAR 6,117,760 mn market cap DB.MetricSaudi Aramco (2222)Peer range P1Key metricsP/E13.86x5.14x (Bahri) to 28.20x (ADES); median of the three peers with a published P/E is 12.43x P1Key metrics P2PeersP/B3.93x1.48x to 2.68x — Aramco is the highest in the set P1Key metrics DBDividend yield5.23%2.78%–2.84% where published P1Key metrics P2PeersROE26.75%−13.86% to 38.98% P1Key metrics DBMarket capSAR 6,117,760 mn766.5 mn to 32,410.49 mn P1Key metrics P2PeersSupporting figures, all as of 2026-10-20 DB:- The National Shipping Company of Saudi Arabia (4030): SAR 35.18, P/E 5.14x, P/B 1.71x, yield 2.84%, ROE 38.98%, cap SAR 32,410.49 mn P2Peers DB- Petro Rabigh (2380): SAR 17.00, P/E 12.43x, P/B 1.66x, yield not published, ROE 17.07%, cap SAR 28,808.04 mn P2Peers DB- ADES Holding Company (2382): SAR 16.20, P/E 28.20x, P/B 2.65x, yield 2.78%, ROE 11.86%, cap SAR 18,573.04 mn P2Peers DB- Arabian Drilling Company (2381): SAR 95.00, P/E not published (EPS unit unconfirmed), P/B 1.48x, yield not published, ROE −3.14%, cap SAR 8,397.15 mn P2Peers DB- Saudi Arabian Refineries Company (2030): SAR 49.80, P/E not published (EPS unit unconfirmed), P/B 2.68x, yield not published, ROE −13.86%, cap SAR 766.5 mn P1Key metrics P2Peers DBAramco's own numbers: price SAR 25.48, P/E 13.86x, P/B 3.93x, EPS TTM SAR 1.84, book value SAR 6.49 per share, yield 5.23%, ROE 26.75%, ROA 15.86% P1Key metrics. Dividend record shows SAR 0.34 per quarter for the three most recent payouts (ex-dates 2026-08-19, 2026-06-01, 2026-03-16), up from SAR 0.33 in 2025 quarters DB.Reading the gap:- Aramco's premium P/B is paired with the second-highest ROE in the set, so it carries a higher book multiple than every peer while only Bahri earns a better return on equity; Bahri's low P/E sits on a much higher EPS-to-price base DB.- The yield gap is the clearest differentiator: Aramco's 5.23% is roughly double the 2.84% and 2.78% of Bahri and ADES, and no peer except those two has a published yield P1Key metricsDB.- Scale is not comparable: Aramco's cap exceeds the five peers combined (SAR 88,955.22 mn) by about 69 times, so the peer set is a sector-exchange grouping rather than like-for-like coverage DB.- Two ratios the comparison would normally include are unavailable here: EV/EBITDA is not applicable for this sector for any name, and no sector percentile ranking is published for P/E, P/B or yield; payout ratio is also unavailable DB.
